summary: Generates or adds a float3 PartForce attribute for Particle POP feedback loops. It combines global force, wind, and local radial, axial, spiral, or planar forces, and can read a specification POP to define many forces from point attributes.

key_params.name: specpop
key_params.note: Optional POP where each point defines a local force with attributes matching parameter names

key_params.name: axial
key_params.note: Enable force along the direction axis

key_params.name: axialr
key_params.note: Axis rotation for the axial force

key_params.name: spiral
key_params.note: Enable spiral force around the direction axis

key_params.name: spiralr
key_params.note: Axis rotation for the spiral force

key_params.name: falloff
key_params.note: Falloff shape such as S curve, bias power, inverse distance, or none

key_params.name: fallofflimitrange
key_params.note: Limit the near range of the falloff

key_params.name: windspeed
key_params.note: Global wind speed converted to force

key_params.name: map0op
key_params.note: Source operator for the first mapping block

key_params.name: map0element
key_params.note: Source element for the first mapping block

key_params.name: map0parm
key_params.note: Target parameter for the first mapping block

key_concepts: Force Radial POP writes or adds to the `PartForce` attribute used by Particle POP-style feedback simulations.
A single node can combine local radial, axial, spiral, and planar forces with global force and wind contributions.
Specification POP points and Map page controls let attributes define many local forces or vary force parameters per point.
common_gotchas: Force Radial POP is a convenience for PartForce; Noise, Math Mix, Lookup, or GLSL POPs can also author PartForce directly.
If PartForce already exists, this operator adds to it, so stacked force nodes accumulate.
For masked forces, use Field POP Weight to scale PartForce instead of assuming the force operator has region masking built in.
